name: Figueira das Lagrimas (Fig Tree of Tears)

location.address: Estrada das Lagrimas 515-537, Sacoma, Ipiranga, Sao Paulo, Brazil

access: Free. Stands in a small fenced public enclosure on an ordinary city street (Estrada das Lagrimas), with plaques; a 2019 municipal revitalisation removed the old surrounding wall specifically to make the tree more approachable to the public.
transport: Sacoma or Ipiranga area, Sao Paulo; nearest CPTM/Metro station is Sacoma (Line 2-Green), roughly 15-20 minutes on foot; check current walking route
verify_notes: Four independent sources fetched directly all agree the tree stands and is alive today: Portuguese Wikipedia, saopauloantiga.com.br (a dedicated local-history piece, checked for a 2024 update), portaldoipiranga.com (2019 revitalisation piece quoting agronomists who monitor the tree's health routinely and note 'good signs of recovery'), and catracalivre.com.br, which calls it 'the oldest documented tree in the city of Sao Paulo'. Officially protected: declared Environmental Heritage of the State of Sao Paulo by Decree 30.443 on 1989-09-20 (immune from cutting), and separately registered as municipal heritage by CONPRESP in 2016 (Resolution 06); one source gives an earlier 1988 protection date, a minor discrepancy not resolved, both recorded. NAME AND HISTORY: on the old road used by soldiers departing for the Paraguayan War (1864-1870), today Estrada das Lagrimas ('Road of Tears'); tradition holds both Dom Pedro I and Dom Pedro II passed it, and it was a farewell point for law students (Faculdade de Direito) and soldiers' families; a Portuguese traveller, Emiliano Zaluar, documented 'its magnificence' in 1861. AGE: no source gives a precise figure with a stated basis; treated as a vague documented age (present and already notable by 1822, so at least two centuries) rather than invented. A search-summary figure of 'approximately 240 years' appeared in one AI search summary but was never found stated on any fetched page, so per the search-summary-is-a-lead-never-a-source rule it is NOT used; recorded here only as a discarded figure. GIRTH/HEIGHT: no source found gives a number; not fabricated, left null. HEALTH HISTORY: the tree was debilitated and faced a removal threat before 1977; a Ficus benjamina sprouted alongside it that year (still present, itself pruned in 2011); necrotic tissue was removed from the trunk in 2001; it is monitored by municipal agronomists. A 2024 retrospective (saopauloantiga.com.br) says the site's 2019 revitalisation 'fell short of what it deserves' (no interpretive signage/QR codes) but confirms the tree itself stands. TRANSPORT: exact station/walk time not independently verified this pass, flagged for a writer/later pass to confirm against a map rather than guessed.
